question: The Sarabanga plan promised bathing-quality water in six months using four small works - which of them can be shown to exist?
intro: This is the leanest action plan on the atlas: no STP, no sewer network - just a 30 KLD faecal-sludge plant, channel filters, a reed-bed and soak pits, totalling Rs 10.6 crore, for a stretch flowing past Edappadi. Seven years on, none of the four works has a public completion record - while the State's 2025-26 policy note declares the river meets bathing standards and TNPCB's own last published reading is BOD 120.

primary.label: TNPCB stretch-wise monthly water-quality reports
primary.note: December 2023 is the last stretch-wise edition TNPCB has published. Every month of 2023 at the stretch station (Edappadi, 3024) was Class E; the final reading was BOD 120 mg/L with zero dissolved oxygen - forty times the bathing target the plan promised within six months.

actionPlan.label: TNPCB Action Plan on Rejuvenation of River Sarabanga (Sept 2019)

baseline.banner: Tamil Nadu publishes no stretch-wise infrastructure progress report - implementation status is reconstructed from NGT case records, official municipal pages and scheme lists. The priority class itself has swung: Priority I (2018, BOD 78) down to Priority II (2022, BOD 24) and back to Priority I (2025, BOD 36 rising to 80 in 2024).
otherSources: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report, October 2025 (mirrored on this site): station 3024 max BOD 36 (2022-23 basis) rising to 80 (2024)
NGT (SZ) judgment in O.A. 51/2015, 27 July 2021 - successor STP DPRs at draft stage; 'no flow' sampling
Idappadi Municipality official site (accessed July 2026): 'There is no underground drainage system in Idappadi Municipality'
TN Environment Dept Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26 - the State's improvement claims

ngt-record.label: NGT (SZ) O.A. 51/2015 judgment, 27.07.2021 - sewage from Edappadi, Omalur and Poolampatti; treatment plants only at draft-DPR stage under Nadanthai Vaazhi Cauvery (WAPCOS); e-flow promised 'after completion by March 2022'

state-claims.label: Environment & Climate Change Dept Policy Note 2024-25 (p.93): BOD in the Sarabanga 'reduced considerably'
Policy Note 2025-26 (p.98): Sarabanga water quality 'is satisfying the bathing standards of CPCB'

regions.name: Idappadi Municipality
regions.inBasinNote: 56,193 people, 5.2 MLD sewage, 22 sullage channels reaching the river; the plan committed treatment for blackwater only.

categories.label: Sewage treatment

actionPlan.summary: No STP or sewer network committed. Instead: a 30 KLD faecal-sludge treatment plant (Rs 4 crore, IUDM 2018-19) by December 2019, and in-situ screen-and-gravel-filter treatment of the 22 sullage channels (Rs 2.5 crore) by December 2019. Blackwater stays in household septic tanks.

mpr.summary: No completion record found anywhere. The municipality's own website (accessed July 2026) states 'there is no underground drainage system' and mentions no FSTP; TWAD Board's completed and ongoing UGSS lists carry no Idappadi or Edappadi entry; the NGT record (July 2021) shows the State proposing new draft-DPR-stage treatment plants under Nadanthai Vaazhi Cauvery instead - with no post-2021 trace of those either.

gaps: Idappadi sits in a politically prominent constituency (Edappadi), yet no sewerage scheme for it appears in any public scheme list through July 2026.
Water-quality outcome at Edappadi station: Class E every month of 2023, ending at BOD 120 in December 2023; CPCB's 2024 maximum was 80.

actionPlan.summary: The plan declares Idappadi's solid-waste system complete ('Proposed Plan of Action: Nil. MSW Treatment Facility provided') - 16 TPD, 100% collection, 86% segregation, 5 micro-composting centres.

mpr.summary: The plan-time claim of completeness has never been re-verified in any public record.

regions.name: Omalur Town Panchayat
regions.inBasinNote: 16,279 people; 11 sewage outfall locations; one mapped riverbank dump of legacy waste.

actionPlan.summary: DPR at Rs 3 crore for treating sullage by 'Reed Bed Filter Technology / Eco Ozotex' under IUDM 2019-20, target March 2020.

mpr.summary: No tender, commissioning or inspection record of the reed-bed plant found in any public source.

actionPlan.summary: Rs 1.1 crore for compound walls, windrow platform and biomining of historical waste dumped along the river, under SBM funds, target December 2019.

regions.name: Thathayampatti & T. Konagapadi Village Panchayats
regions.inBasinNote: Together ~9,000 people; K.R. Thoppur habitation had 550 households draining directly to the river.

actionPlan.summary: Individual and community soak pits under MGNREGS 2019-20, target July 2019 - including the 550 river-connected households of K.R. Thoppur. 'After construction of soak pits no waste water will be disposed into the river.'

mpr.summary: No completion record found in any public source.

regions.name: Industry on the stretch (sago, granite, dyeing)
regions.inBasinNote: 93 units in the riverside taluks per the plan's annexure, including 4 consented sago factories; the plan asserts no industrial discharge.

categories.label: Industrial effluent

actionPlan.summary: 'No highly polluting industries located along the polluted river stretch... no industrial discharge.' Two sago units consented for on-land disposal, two for inland surface water (stated as non-operational). No dyeing unit appears anywhere in the plan.

mpr.summary: CPCB's official 2025 description of this stretch is 'Sarabanga at Edapadi, downstream of TEXTILE DYEING INDUSTRIES effluent' - the industry the 2019 plan never mentioned is now in the stretch's very name. The 2019 baseline sampling had already found copper, zinc and nickel at Edappadi.

gaps: No public inventory reconciles the plan's 'no industrial discharge' with CPCB's dyeing-effluent designation - which units, since when, under what consent?
